meta.sponsor: Pfizer (with Diabetes UK and the UK Department of Health)
meta.mechanism: HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor (statin); lowers LDL-C (~40% at 10 mg/day)
meta.indication: primary prevention of major cardiovascular events in type 2 diabetes without prior cardiovascular disease and without high LDL-C (LDL-C <=4.14 mmol/L), with at least one further risk factor (hypertension, retinopathy, albuminuria or current smoking)

n_randomized.quote: 2838 patients aged 40-75 years in 132 centres in the UK and Ireland were randomised to placebo (n=1410) or atorvastatin 10 mg daily (n=1428).
n_randomized.note: Design paper S4 abstract (2002, before readout): 'The trial includes 2838 men and women aged 40-75 years.' FDA label S7 gives 1429 atorvastatin / 1411 placebo; registry S3 lists enrollment 2800. Pfizer release S2: 'roughly 2,800 patients'.

median_followup.quote: Median duration of follow-up was 3.9 years (IQR 3.0-4.7).
median_followup.note: CTT 2010 Table 1 (S8) gives median follow-up in survivors 4.1 years. Planned duration was longer: S1 'terminated 2 years earlier than expected'.

primary_endpoint.value: Time to first acute CHD event (MI including silent MI, unstable angina, acute CHD death, resuscitated cardiac arrest), coronary revascularisation, or stroke
primary_endpoint.quote: The primary endpoint was time to first occurrence of the following: acute coronary heart disease events, coronary revascularisation, or stroke.
primary_endpoint.note: Component detail from S6: 'acute CHD event (i.e. myocardial infarction including silent infarction, unstable angina, acute CHD death, resuscitated cardiac arrest), coronary revascularisation procedures, or stroke.'

inclusion_key_criteria.value: Type 2 diabetes, age 40-75, no documented CVD, LDL-C <=4.14 mmol/L (160 mg/dL), fasting TG <=6.78 mmol/L (600 mg/dL), plus >=1 of retinopathy, albuminuria, current smoking or hypertension
inclusion_key_criteria.quote: Study entrants had no documented previous history of cardiovascular disease, an LDL-cholesterol concentration of 4.14 mmol/L or lower, a fasting triglyceride amount of 6.78 mmol/L or less, and at least one of the following: retinopathy, albuminuria, current smoking, or hypertension.
inclusion_key_criteria.note: Same criteria in design paper S4 abstract (pub 2002) and registry S3 eligibility (age 40-75).

planned_events.quote: Patients will be followed until 304 primary endpoints have accrued (expected date early 2005).
planned_events.note: Read in abstract only (Wiley full text not accessible). Consistent with S6: 'This first interim analysis was triggered by the accrual of 25% of the total expected endpoints (76) in October 2000.' (76 = 25% of 304). Trial stopped with 210 primary events (69% of planned).

assumed_rrr.note: NOT FOUND. The design assumption on event reduction was not in any text read. S6 states the power calculation assumed a 30% LDL-C difference: 'the difference in LDL cholesterol between the active and placebo treatments was -40% rather than the value of -30% on which the power calculation had been based.' The Lancet full text (S1, paywalled) probably states the assumed risk reduction.

power.quote: Whilst, like most trials, CARDS was powered at 90%, predicting a much later termination date, in reality there was substantial power to detect significant treatment effects earlier in the follow-up period, which was one of the purposes of specifying early stopping rules.

alpha.unit: two-sided (final analysis threshold after interim looks)
alpha.quote: The p values are considered significant at conventional levels (p<0.05) for effects other than those on the primary endpoint, for which p<0.049 was considered significant to allow for interim analysis effects on the type 1 error rate.
alpha.note: Interim early-stopping threshold was much stricter: S6 'it was not sufficient to meet the stringent early stopping threshold (p<0.001)'; S5 'because of the clear benefit of active treatment (two-tailed p < 0.001)'; S14 (Scheen 2003) gives the stopping threshold as one-sided p<0.0005. Sidedness of 0.049 not stated explicitly; two-sided assumed (S5 analyses were 'two-sided').

stopped_early.quote: The trial was terminated 2 years earlier than expected because the prespecified early stopping rule for efficacy had been met.
stopped_early.note: Stopped for benefit at the second prespecified interim analysis (S6: 'CARDS was terminated almost 2 years earlier than planned because at the second pre-scheduled interim analysis the data-safety-monitoring board found a highly significant benefit with treatment beyond that stipulated in the early stopping rule.'). First interim (76 events, Oct 2000) was already p=0.03. Final count 210 of 304 planned primary events. Decision announced 16 June 2003 (S2).

genetics.finding: Mendelian randomization: HMGCR (statin target) LDL-lowering variants protect against cardiovascular events, with the same effect per unit LDL-C as PCSK9 variants
genetics.effect: OR 0.81 (0.72-0.90) per 10 mg/dL lower LDL-C for the HMGCR score
genetics.quote: Variants in PCSK9 and HMGCR were associated with nearly identical protective effects on the risk of cardiovascular events per decrease of 10 mg per deciliter (0.26 mmol per liter) in the LDL cholesterol level: odds ratio for cardiovascular events, 0.81 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.74 to 0.89) for PCSK9 and 0.81 (95% CI, 0.72 to 0.90) for HMGCR.

genetics.finding: HMGCR LDL-lowering variants mimic statins and slightly raise type 2 diabetes risk and body weight (on-target effect); not a CV-harm signal
genetics.effect: rs17238484-G: LDL-C -0.06 mmol/L per allele; T2D OR 1.02 (1.00-1.05)
genetics.quote: The rs17238484-G allele seemed to be associated with higher risk of type 2 diabetes (odds ratio [OR] per allele 1·02, 95% CI 1·00-1·05); the rs12916-T allele association was consistent (1·06, 1·03-1·09).

genetics.finding: EAS consensus: genetic, epidemiologic and trial evidence unequivocally establishes LDL as causal for ASCVD
genetics.effect: risk reduction proportional to absolute LDL-C reduction and duration
genetics.quote: Consistent evidence from numerous and multiple different types of clinical and genetic studies unequivocally establishes that LDL causes ASCVD.

genetics.finding: CTT: major vascular events reduced ~22% per 1 mmol/L LDL-C reduction (benchmark for the calculator)
genetics.quote: When both types of trial were combined, similar proportional reductions in major vascular events per 1·0 mmol/L LDL cholesterol reduction were found in all types of patient studied (rate ratio [RR] 0·78, 95% CI 0·76–0·80; p<0·0001)

genetics.finding: CTT diabetes meta-analysis: in 18,686 people with diabetes, statins reduce major vascular events by 21% per mmol/L LDL-C, as in people without diabetes
genetics.quote: There was a significant 21% proportional reduction in major vascular events per mmol/L reduction in LDL cholesterol in people with diabetes (0.79, 0.72-0.86; p<0.0001), which was similar to the effect observed in those without diabetes (0.79, 0.76-0.82; p<0.0001).

consensus_explanation.summary: CARDS tested atorvastatin 10 mg in type 2 diabetes without cardiovascular disease and without high LDL-C (mean baseline 3.0 mmol/L). It lowered LDL-C by about 41% (about 1.1 mmol/L at 1 year) and cut first major cardiovascular events by 37% (83 vs 127 patients; HR 0.63, 95% CI 0.48-0.83, p=0.001). The trial was stopped about 2 years early at its second interim analysis, with 210 of 304 planned events, because the prespecified efficacy stopping rule was met. The investigators concluded that no LDL-C threshold justifies withholding statins in type 2 diabetes, so the question becomes whether any patients are at low enough risk to go without one. They put the effect, larger than planned, partly down to a 40% rather than the assumed 30% LDL-C difference. The CTT diabetes meta-analysis (2008) found the same 21% reduction per mmol/L in diabetes as in other patients and backed statins for all diabetic people at sufficient risk; later HMGCR Mendelian randomization and the EAS consensus confirmed the target and the biomarker. Caveats from the authors and commentators: the early stop meant fewer events, all-cause mortality was only borderline (27%, p=0.059), and the 48% stroke reduction was not explained by lipoprotein changes.

open_questions: Assumed relative risk reduction behind the 304-event / 90% power design: NOT FOUND (Lancet full text and design-paper full text not accessible). S6 says only that the power calculation assumed a 30% LDL-C difference.
Absolute placebo-adjusted LDL-C change: CTT 2010 gives -1.14 mmol/L at 1 year (used); secondary summaries give 1.2 mmol/L and 46 mg/dL. The Lancet paper's own figure was not read.
On-treatment non-HDL-C and triglyceride differences: NOT FOUND.
Alpha: final threshold p<0.049 (S6) after interim looks; the interim stopping boundary was p<0.001 (S6), stated as one-sided p<0.0005 by Scheen (S14). Sidedness of 0.049 assumed two-sided.

Observed HR 0.63 is lower than the CTT per-mmol/L prediction (0.78^1.14 = 0.75, derived). Likely reasons: truncation for benefit at an interim analysis (210 of 304 planned events), wide CI (0.48-0.83), and a larger LDL-C contrast than designed. S5 found stroke reduction (48%) not explained by lipoprotein changes.

Readout date: the stop decision was announced 16 June 2003 (Pfizer release S2, citing a UCL announcement). Full results came later (ADA June 2004; Lancet August 2004). The Wayback capture of the release is dated 2003-06-23.
The registry record (S3) was first posted in 2006, after the trial ended (retrospective registration). It lists enrollment 2800, against 2838 randomised in the paper.
Lancet commentary 'Statins for all patients with type 2 diabetes: not so soon' (S18) not read; its arguments are not reflected here beyond its title.

FIELD (the first-choice case) was not built: no ClinicalTrials.gov NCT record found (API v2 searches for 'FIELD fenofibrate', 'Fenofibrate Intervention and Event Lowering', ISRCTN64783481, and fenofibrate + type 2 diabetes studies starting before 2003 or enrolling >3000 returned no FIELD record; FIELD is registered only as ISRCTN64783481). CARDS was the first fallback with an NCT record and a readable topline announcement.
